parsed.attack: The buyer and the sufferer are different people. The financial-POA sibling doing the Excel rebuild is discharging a duty, while the sibling who actually feels pain about the money is the medical-POA one who suspects and is not paying - so a product whose output is voluntary transparency is being sold to the party with the least appetite for producing it. In practice most POA holders keep no contemporaneous record at all; they reconstruct at formal accounting or estate settlement, which is why the felt need is one or two acute weeks at the end rather than a monthly subscription, and [211] is one description of doing the job in Excel, not evidence anyone has paid to stop.
parsed.strongest_defence: Fiduciary duty is non-discretionary and personally liable - a POA holder can be surcharged for an unexplained line - so the monthly statement is not transparency the buyer chooses but documentation they are obliged to be able to produce, and the exportable record is what makes two years of accumulated history too expensive to abandon.
parsed.verdict_reason: A genuine legal obligation sits underneath, but the pain is episodic and concentrated at the end, and the person who feels it most is not the person being asked to pay.
